entities.summary:
Philippe de Luxembourg was a French cardinal and bishop, born in the 15th century, who played a significant role in the Catholic Church during the Late Middle Ages. He was the Archbishop of Reims from 1503 until his death in 1519 and was a key figure in the French Reformation. Philippe de Luxembourg was a prominent advisor to King Louis XII of France and played a crucial role in shaping the country's religious and political landscape during the 16th century. He was also a patron of the arts and architecture, and his influence can be seen in the construction of many notable buildings and monuments throughout France. Philippe de Luxembourg's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he played a key role in shaping the course of French history and the Catholic Church. He was a true Renaissance man, exceling in both the spiritual and temporal realms.

He was a member of the Order of the Golden Fleece and was appointed as the Duke of Orléans by King Louis XII. Philippe de Luxembourg was also a skilled diplomat and strategist, and his efforts helped to secure the peace between France and its neighboring countries. He was a strong advocate for the rights of the Church and the protection of its interests.

Philippe de Luxembourg's impact on French history cannot be overstated. He played a key role in shaping the country's religious and political landscape during the 16th century, and his influence can still be felt today. He was a true leader and statesman, who left an indelible mark on French society and culture.

One of the most notable achievements of Philippe de Luxembourg was his role in the French Reformation. He was a strong advocate for reform within the Catholic Church, and his efforts helped to shape the course of the Reformation in France. He was a key figure in the development of the Council of Trent, which aimed to reform the Catholic Church and address the concerns of the Protestant Reformation.
